meta.depth_rule: A strategy sits at the deepest level its whole wording supports: the family when it names only the domain, the mechanism when it names the lever (plan_words), the pathway when it names the causal channel (text_cues) and no sibling. No invented specificity.

subpillars.name: Tackling Structural Exclusion
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that address the exclusion of specific groups, including women, youth, informal workers, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities, as well as the structural barriers that limit their opportunities, such as discrimination, unequal access to services and resources, limited voice and participation, and lack of protection of rights and dignity. Formalisation of informal workers belongs here, including registration, labour contracts, labour rights, and social insurance or pension coverage.

subpillars.name: Enhancing Capabilities
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that expand people's capabilities to lead healthy, productive, and resilient lives, including through education, skills, digital access, health, social protection, food security, livelihoods, and basic services. This category is intentionally broad enough to include areas that may otherwise fall under 'human security,' avoiding an artificial distinction between capability-building and protection from vulnerability.

subpillars.name: Future Generations
subpillars.definition: Covers whether today's strategies protect long-term well-being and avoid shifting risks or costs onto future generations, including through climate resilience, just transition, nature and biodiversity, sustainable resource use, intergenerational equity and responsible public finance.

subpillars.name: Export-led
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that grow the economy through external markets, including export promotion and diversification, trade agreements and market access, foreign direct investment, international tourism, trade logistics, and the innovation and technology upgrading that make traded sectors competitive.

subpillars.name: Domestic Integration
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that strengthen links within the domestic economy, including local value chains and value addition, agro-processing, industrial clusters, and connections between regions and between rural and urban markets.

subpillars.name: Growth through Inclusion
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that create jobs and incomes for groups left out of growth, including women, youth, informal workers and rural households, through enterprise development, MSME support, productivity, finance and market access. Formalisation of informal businesses belongs here, including registration, licensing, and access to finance and markets.

subpillars.name: Anticipation and Strategic Foresight
subpillars.definition: Focuses on the ability of governments to identify and prepare for future risks, opportunities and disruptions, including through horizon scanning, scenario planning, early warning, contingency planning, risk-informed analysis, and future-oriented strategy.

subpillars.name: Adaptability and Course Correction
subpillars.definition: Refers to the capacity to adjust priorities, policies, plans, and investments in response to new evidence, changing conditions or shifting development needs. This includes institutional flexibility, learning by doing, revising strategies, and making timely course corrections.

subpillars.name: Agility and Delivery Capability
subpillars.definition: Captures the ability of institutions to act quickly and effectively, mobilize resources, coordinate across government, implement reforms and respond to shocks or emerging priorities without major disruption.

subpillars.name: Reform Leadership, Coalitions and Civic Engagement
subpillars.definition: Covers strategies that build the political, institutional, and social support needed to advance reform, including political will, reform incentives, collaborative leadership, coalitions, public-private collaboration, civic participation, and co-creation.
